newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: IBCA reaffirms Sappi domestic ratings.
newsitem.headline: IBCA reaffirms Sappi domestic ratings.

text.p: Rating agency IBCA on Monday reaffirmed South African pulp and paper producer Sappi Ltd's short-term "A1" and long-term "A" domestic ratings.
The agency said the ratings reflected a low expectation of investment risk and a strong capacity for timely repayment of interest and principal.
IBCA noted that as a forestry products group, Sappi's performance was inherently susceptible to the cyclical tendencies of the sector.

"However, the relatively high degree of vertical integration, particularly in its southern African operations, the breadth of product range as well as its increasing international profile provide a large measure of risk diversification to the group's business profile," the agency said.
Sappi's financial profile had suffered from the collapse in paper and pulp prices since 1996, coupled with escalating financing costs.
"Earnings and cash flows are highly margin sensitive, with the level of fixed capital and acquisitional investment critical to net cash flows.
"Nonetheless, the underlying cash generative capacity remains strong, evidenced by consistently positive internal cash flow."
The outlook for the group's main product markets appeared more positive than negative, with the rate of recovery expected to be gradual in the near-term before accelerating later in 1998, it added.
